title: Plate Tectonics
text: Plate tectonics is the scientific theory describing the large-scale motion of seven major and several minor plates of the Earth's lithosphere. The theory, which developed in the 1960s, explains the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes, the creation of mountain ranges, and the arrangement of continents and oceans. Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, noting that the coastlines of South America and Africa appear to fit together. Plates move at rates of a few centimeters per year. Where plates converge, one may subduct beneath another, creating volcanic arcs and deep ocean trenches. Where they diverge, new oceanic crust forms at mid-ocean ridges.
